content: Mefloquine is indicated for the treatment of mild-to-moderate acute malaria caused by mefloquine-susceptible strains of Plasmodium falciparum (both chloroquine-susceptible and resistant strains) or Plasmodium vivax. The recommended dosage is 1250 mg orally as a single dose. For prophylaxis, 250 mg orally once weekly should be initiated 1–2 weeks prior to entering an endemic area and continued for 4 weeks after leaving the area. If a full treatment course does not result in clinical improvement within 48–72 hours, mefloquine should not be used for retreatment, and an alternative therapy should be considered. Similarly, if prophylaxis with mefloquine has previously failed, it should not be used for curative treatment. There is insufficient clinical data to establish the efficacy of mefloquine in malaria caused by Plasmodium ovale or Plasmodium malariae. Patients with acute P. vivax malaria treated with mefloquine are at high risk of relapse because the drug does not eliminate exoerythrocytic (hepatic phase) parasites. To prevent relapse, patients should receive subsequent treatment with an 8-aminoquinoline derivative, such as primaquine, after the initial treatment of the acute infection with mefloquine. Mefloquine should be taken with food and at least 8 ounces of water. If vomiting occurs, the full or partial dose may be repeated. Drug Interactions and Contraindications: 1. Lefamulin: Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation, which may lead to torsades de pointes, other serious arrhythmias, or sudden death. If coadministration is unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 2. Afatinib: Mefloquine increases afatinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the afatinib dose by 10 mg daily if not tolerated. 3. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Amisulpride: Both amisulpride and mefloquine prolong the QT interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
